title_en: Cen Chaozuo and Cen Shubai — case of sabotaging elections
keywords_en: Criminal; Undermining Elections; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Guangdong Province; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Whether Vote-Buying Constitutes the Crime of Undermining Elections; Determination of Principal and Accessory; Ruling for Plaintiff; Bribing People's Congress Deputies; Town Mayor Election; Bribery in Elections; Accepting Bribes; Offering Bribes
full_text_en:
Cen Chaozuo and Cen Shubai — Election Sabotage Case

Defendant: Cen Chaozuo, male, 49 years old, Han ethnicity, from Enping City, Guangdong Province, self-employed, residing at No. 6 Xinxijiang Road, Jiangzhou Town, Enping City. Arrested on December 3, 1994.

Defendant: Cen Shubai, male, 48 years old, Han ethnicity, from Enping City, Guangdong Province, formerly deputy manager of Yuezhou Metal Products Co., Ltd. of Jiangzhou Town, Enping City, residing at No. 3 Nonglin Street, Jiangzhou Town. Arrested on December 3, 1994.

The defendants Cen Chaozuo and Cen Shubai were prosecuted for election sabotage by the People's Procuratorate of Enping City, Guangdong Province, before the Enping City People's Court. After accepting the case, the Enping City People's Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and, upon trial, found the following facts:

In mid-August 1994, upon learning that a by-election for the town mayor of Jiangzhou Town, Enping City, would be held on September 13 of the same year, the defendant Cen Chaozuo conceived of bribing the town People's Congress representatives to secure his election as the town mayor of Jiangzhou Town. Thereafter, the defendant Cen Chaozuo, in collusion with the defendant Cen Shubai, repeatedly assembled Cen Jinliang, Cen Junling, Cen Lianheng, Cen Qiaoci, and Zhang Weilian (five persons, all dealt with separately) at the Haijingfang Restaurant in Jiangzhou Town and at Cen Chaozuo's home, where they conspired and planned to bribe the 11th-term town People's Congress representatives of Jiangzhou Town, so that the representatives would vote for Cen Chaozuo as the town mayor. Cen Chaozuo expressed willingness to use his own money to bribe the representatives, and Cen Shubai expressed willingness to actively assist Cen Chaozuo in bribing representatives from the Dongbei Yan Management District, Yonghua Management District, Zhong'an Management District, Jinjiang Sugar Factory, and other entities. They agreed that bribing at least half of the 47 town People's Congress representatives was necessary to ensure Cen Chaozuo's election as town mayor. On September 10 of the same year, the two defendants notified Cen Jinliang and the other four persons to gather at Cen Chaozuo's home, where they handed over 22 envelopes, each containing RMB 1,000 prepared in advance by Cen Chaozuo, to Cen Jinliang and the other four persons. Subsequently, Cen Jinliang and the other four separately bribed the town People's Congress representatives with whom they had connections, asking the representatives to vote for Cen Chaozuo as town mayor. Cen Chaozuo personally bribed six representatives. The total amount of bribes distributed was RMB 34,500. On September 13, the 3rd Session of the 11th People's Congress of Jiangzhou Town was convened for the by-election of the town mayor. The election result was: of the 47 representatives who voted, the town mayor candidate Cen Jinyuan received 23 votes, Cen Chaozuo received 15 votes, 6 invalid votes had the name "Cen Chaozuo" written on them, and there were 2 abstentions. Due to the bribery actions of Cen Chaozuo and Cen Shubai, the town mayor election could not be lawfully conducted. After the case was solved, RMB 24,700 of the bribe money was recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by the confessions of the co-defendants and the bribe recipients, witness testimony, photographs of physical evidence, and the recovered bribe money; both defendants also confessed to the charges.

The Enping City People's Court held that the defendants Cen Chaozuo and Cen Shubai, disregarding national laws and violating the provisions of the Election Law, for the purpose of enabling Cen Chaozuo to be elected as town mayor, adopted the illegal method of bribing the town People's Congress representatives with money to sabotage the election, obstructing the voters' free exercise of the right to vote and the right to stand for election, causing the serious consequence that the 3rd Session of the 11th People's Congress of Jiangzhou Town could not elect the town mayor, and the social harm was significant. Their actions constituted the crime of sabotage of elections as provided in Article 142 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. In accordance with Article 22 of the Criminal Law, the actions of Cen Chaozuo and Cen Shubai constituted joint intentional crime. In the joint crime, Cen Chaozuo played the role of organizer and plotter, providing funds to bribe the People's Congress representatives, and according to Article 23 of the Criminal Law, he was the principal offender in this case and should be given a heavier punishment; Cen Shubai participated in the plotting and actively helped Cen Chaozuo carry out the crime, and according to Article 24 of the Criminal Law, he was an accessory in this case and should be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offender. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, the recovered bribe money used for the crime should be confiscated. Accordingly, on January 9, 1995, the Enping City People's Court, on conviction of sabotage of elections, respectively sentenced Cen Chaozuo to fixed-term imprisonment of two years and Cen Shubai to fixed-term imprisonment of one year. The bribe money of RMB 24,700 transferred with the case was confiscated and turned over to the national treasury.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, neither defendant appealed.
